ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Engineering
Requirements: To apply as a first-year student, you will need to submit the following: a completed application (either the Common Application or the Clarkson Application), your official high school transcript, and one letter of recommendation (from a school counselor, teacher or someone who can speak to your academic potential).
Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering
Description:
The Bachelor of Science in Aeronautical Engineering at Clarkson is a multidisciplinary program with a special focus on the design of aircraft and spacecraft. You'll gain a strong foundation in aerodynamics, flight dynamics and control, propulsion and structures.

You will have opportunities for hands-on experience through our design-based curriculum and with our SPEED (Student Projects for Engineering Experience and Design) teams, like the Design, Build, Fly team, which regularly places high in international competitions.

You will be prepared for a successful career in the aerospace industry or for advanced graduate study.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is www.clarkson.edu.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Department: Wallace H. Coulter School of Engineering
Description:
Aerospace engineers apply scientific principles and engineering concepts to design, build and test aircraft, spacecraft, satellites and missiles. They also test prototypes to make sure that they function according to plans. This work can be analytical, computational, or hands-on. At Clarkson, you will learn and work in all three areas.

Clarkson's Bachelor of Science in Aerospace Engineering degree program combines an interdisciplinary core curriculum with specialized aerospace coursework. As an aerospace engineering major, you will acquire a strong foundation in mathematics and the physical sciences. You will take courses in the fundamental engineering disciplines of solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, thermodynamics and materials science. You'll then progress to a challenging curriculum of advanced aerospace topics, including aerodynamics, aerospace structures, flight dynamics, and propulsion. You'll take at least two advanced aerospace electives, one of which will be a lab course, and two other technical electives. With the help of a faculty advisor, you'll be able to tailor your electives to fit your career interests. In your final year, you'll participate in a yearlong, team-based capstone design experience, in which you'll work with a team to complete a comprehensive design project.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is www.clarkson.edu.
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science degree in aerospace engineering is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics and Statistics
Requirements: Clarkson requires the following from first-year applicants: a completed Common Application or Clarkson Application, an official high school transcript, and one letter of recommendation.
Description: Applied mathematics and statistics focus on the creation and study of mathematical and computational tools that can be used to solve a range of scientific, engineering and other problems. Applications can be found in a diverse array of fields, from the traditional sciences to the social sciences. The applied mathematics and statistics program at Clarkson has strengths in dynamical systems, optimization, statistics, and computational and data-enabled science and engineering. Through this program, students develop a strong fundamental background in core mathematics, as well as expertise in an application area of their choice. Graduates are well-prepared for professional careers in industry and government and are ready for graduate study in an applied mathematics, statistics, data science or other scientific or engineering discipline.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official university website for Clarkson University is www.clarkson.edu.

Requirements: A completed Common Application or Clarkson Application (we have no preference), an official high school transcript, and one letter of recommendation from your school counselor or a teacher.
Description:
Biochemistry lies at the intersection of biology and chemistry. It is the study of the molecular basis of life. As a biochemist, you'll explore the chemical processes that occur in living organisms, from viruses and bacteria to plants and animals. Our biochemistry major at Clarkson provides you with a strong foundation in the principles of chemistry, biology and physics, with a focus on their application to biological systems. You will gain a deep understanding of the structure, function and regulation of biomolecules, such as proteins, nucleic acids and lipids. You will also learn how these molecules interact to carry out the complex processes of life.

Our program is distinctive in several ways. We emphasize hands-on learning, with extensive laboratory experience integrated throughout the curriculum. You will have the opportunity to work with state-of-the-art instrumentation and techniques, preparing you for a career in research, medicine, biotechnology or other related fields. You will also have the opportunity to participate in cutting-edge research alongside our faculty members, who are experts in their fields. Our research areas include cancer biology, drug discovery, protein engineering and environmental biochemistry. This research experience is invaluable for students who plan to pursue graduate or professional school.

Description: Clarkson's biology major is designed to provide you with the best possible preparation for a career in the health professions, graduate research and education. All of our pre-health-profession students have the opportunity to get involved in our pre-health advising program, where they gain the experience necessary for success in their chosen field. Clarkson's biology major requires 35 credit hours in biology, including coursework in genetics, ecology, and cell and molecular biology. Students can choose advanced electives in a variety of areas. Most biology majors participate in a research project in collaboration with a faculty member. Our students have been accepted to many top medical schools. Recent graduates have also found rewarding jobs at biotech companies and government agencies or pursued advanced degrees in graduate school.
